etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English begynner, equivalent to begin +‎ -er. Cognate with West Frisian begjinner (“beginner”), Dutch beginner (“beginner”), Low German begünner (“beginner”), Danish nybegynder (“beginner, novice”, literally “new-beginner”).

definitions.definition: Someone who is just starting at something, or has only recently started.
Someone who sets something in motion.
(theater) An actor who is present on stage in the first moments of a play.

quote.citation: 1949, Walter Macqueen-Pope, Gaiety: Theatre of Enchantment, page 60:
quote.text: On the stage, the beginners for the first piece had taken their places — the chorus were there, scared but determined, and in the wings waited Harlequin, in the person of Charles Lyall  […]
